chunks: Al-Husayn ibn Said from Ibn Abi Umayr from Ibn Udhaynah from Zurarah from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) who said:

He said: 'When a man catches part of the prayer and misses part behind an Imam, he counts the prayer behind him. He makes the first part he caught as the first of his prayer. If he catches two rak'ahs from Dhuhr, or Asr, or Isha, and two rak'ahs are missed for him, he recites in each rak'ah that he caught behind the Imam, in himself, with Umm al-Kitab and a Surah. If he does not catch the Surah completely, Umm al-Kitab suffices for him. When the Imam gives the salam, he stands and prays two rak'ahs, not reciting in them, because recitation in the prayer is only in the first two from each rak'ah with Umm al-Kitab and a Surah, and in the last two, no recitation is done in them; rather, it is glorification, takbir, tahlil, and supplication, without recitation. And if he catches one rak'ah, he recites in it behind the Imam. When the Imam gives the salam, he stands and recites with Umm al-Kitab and a Surah, then sits and testifies (tashahhud), then stands and prays two rak'ahs in which there is no recitation.'

key_terms.أُمُّ الْكِتَابِ: Umm al-Kitab (The Mother of the Book), referring to Surah Al-Fatihah

ai.seo_question: How does a worshipper complete their prayer if they join late behind the Imam and miss some rak'ahs?
ai.summary: This hadith from Shaykh al-Tusi’s *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* establishes the jurisprudential principle that a follower (muqtadi) joining late prayer counts the caught rak'ahs as the first, thereby determining the obligation of recitation based on whether those rak'ahs fall within the first two or the last two of the prayer. It clarifies the Shia view that recitation of *Umm al-Kitab* and a Surah is required in the first two rak'ahs of the follower's completed prayer, while the final two are performed with silence and glorification, reflecting the distinct legal methodology of the Ahl al-Bayt school. This ruling underscores the importance of following the Imam's actions while maintaining the structural integrity of the individual's prayer unit.
